Cc: Acme Security Team <security@acme.com>
Date: Mon, 19 Jul 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Per-tenant retention & EU storage for Acme app

Hi Aditya / Marissa,

Thanks for taking this. We’re in the final stages of a procurement review and need clarity on two related capabilities before legal signs off:

1) Per-tenant configurable retention TTLs (we need the ability to set retention at tenant-level with options down to 30 days and up to 7 years).
2) Region-bound storage: all data for specific tenants MUST reside in the EU (data-at-rest), including backups and any cold snapshots.

Attached is a short requirements spreadsheet (acme-retention-requirements.xlsx) and a CSV with the object map we’d expect you to purge (requested-data-map.csv). Key asks:
- Acceptance criteria we can include in the SOW (what does “EU-only” cover technically and operationally?)
- Deletion SLA: ability to fully purge an account within a confirmed window (we’re asking for 72 hours or less across all layers)
- Audit evidence: logs and proof-of-deletion artifacts we can share with our auditors
- Timeline for a rollout and any migration plan for existing tenants

If you can cc engineering and send a short roadmap + list of unknowns by end of week, that would be ideal. Happy to hop on a 30m sync if helpful.

Thanks,
Darren

Subject: Re: Configurable retention + regional storage - technical feasibility notes

Aditya / team — quick technical readout based on Darren’s sheet and initial doc:

Design options (pros/cons):
- Tenant-tagged EU buckets per customer (S3 or equivalent): straightforward separation, simple lifecycle rules. Effort: small for new tenants, moderate to migrate existing tenants.
- Single multi-tenant EU bucket with tenant prefix + strict IAM + per-tenant encryption keys: lower operational footprint but higher blast radius risk and more complex audits.
- Region-aware routing layer (request-level) that pins read/write to EU-backed storage and routes KV cache misses to EU-only nodes: best for low-latency, but requires more infra changes.

Deletion and snapshots:
- We can implement an immediate logical deletion that enqueues physical purge jobs. Worst-case purge across backups/snapshots could take longer; to meet 72 hours we need a targeted migration of snapshot retention windows for EU-only tenants first.
- Proposed SLA achievable: 72 hours for logical + background purge; 24-72 hours physical purge depending on snapshot cadence.

Impact areas / engineering tasks (rough):
- Storage topology changes + tenancy tagging (3-4 engineer-weeks)
- Backup and snapshot policy extension for region-bound tenants (2-3 engineer-weeks)
- Deletion pipeline and audit artifacts (logs, signed receipts) (2 engineer-weeks)
- KMS key separation & key-rotation policy (1-2 engineer-weeks)
- Test matrix and e2e QA (1-2 engineer-weeks)

Open questions:
- Does Acme require per-tenant KMS keys? (this affects lead time)
- Any regulatory certification evidence (SOC2 appendix) needed for this change beyond audit logs?

I’ll drop the rough task breakdown into JIRA-ENG-9345 and tag owners. If we prioritize this to the start of Q4 we can have a pilot for a few tenants in ~10 weeks.

— Karthik
Lead Systems Engineer, Redwood Inference

Thanks everyone — summary and proposed acceptance criteria I’ll send to Acme tomorrow, but capturing it here for alignment: 

High level (product):
- Per-tenant retention settings exposed in the tenant admin API (min 30 days, max 7 years)
- Tenant-level storage residency flag that guarantees primary + backups are provisioned in EU regions only for flagged tenants
- Deletion SLA: logical deletion confirmed within 24 hours; physical purge across live data and applicable backups within 72 hours.
- Audit artifacts: immutable deletion receipt (timestamp, operator, vaulted-hash) and retention-change history exportable as CSV/JSON

Acceptance criteria (SOW language draft):
- When tenant X requests purge, Redwood will provide deletion receipt within 24 hours and complete purge within 72 hours except where extended by mutually agreed operational constraints.
- All data for tenant X will be provisioned and stored in EU-only storage; backups used to restore tenant X will not leave EU unless explicitly requested and documented.
- Redwood will provide access to deletion logs for a period of 2 years for audit purposes.

Next steps / owners: 
- Karthik: add detailed task list & effort estimates to JIRA-ENG-9345 (ETA Wed COB)
- Soojin: impact analysis on serving runtime and cache invalidation (ETA Wed COB)
- Aditya: deliver SOW-ready acceptance criteria to Darren tomorrow; coordinate legal/CS
- Marissa: prioritize in roadmap — request Q4 pilot readiness; follow up with Acme on per-tenant KMS question.

Darren — any objections to the AC above or adjustments for legal language? If not, I’ll post this to the working doc and create the Jira ticket this afternoon.

Thanks — Marissa
